learningObjectives: Explain how JPA and Hibernate map Java objects to database tables.
Create entity and repository relationships for persistent data.
Construct a basic CRUD workflow using Spring Data JPA.

activities.title: JPA Persistence Architecture
activities.instruction: Explore how application objects reach the database.

content.concept: Spring Data JPA provides repository abstractions over JPA, while Hibernate is a commonly used JPA provider that handles object-relational mapping between Java entities and relational database data.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Contains the application logic that uses persistent data.
Provides repository abstractions for common persistence operations.
Defines standard APIs and annotations for object-relational persistence.
Implements JPA functionality and maps entity objects to relational data.
Stores persistent records in tables and relationships.

activities.title: JPA Entity Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the important parts of a JPA entity.

content.concept: A JPA entity is a Java class mapped to persistent data. Common annotations identify the entity and its primary key, while fields represent persistent attributes.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Marks the class as a JPA entity.
Defines the Java object whose instances can be persisted.
Represents persistent data such as name, email, or age.
Provides a constructor that JPA can use when creating entity instances.

activities.title: Repository Builder
activities.instruction: Build a Spring Data repository for an entity.

content.concept: Spring Data repositories provide ready-to-use persistence operations such as saving, finding, and deleting entities. Repository interfaces can also define derived query methods.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

content.concept: Spring Data JPA repositories expose operations for creating or updating entities, retrieving them, and deleting them from persistent storage.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

goal: 1. Create or modify an entity object
2. Save the entity through the repository
3. Retrieve entity data with a repository query
4. Modify the retrieved entity when needed
5. Delete the entity through the repository when required
